{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that harmonic tones paired with a subject's own name (CS+) would elicit larger late event-related potential positivity components (P3b and LTW amplitude) compared to tones paired with different names (CS-).",
  "design": "between/within",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Classical conditioning pairing two harmonic tones (CS+ and CS-) with a participant's own name (SON) versus different names (DN) as unconditioned stimuli.",
  "outcome_measure": "Event-Related Brain Potentials (ERPs), specifically P3b and LTW (Late Time Window) amplitudes measured from midline electrodes (Fz, Cz, Pz).",
  "population_and_setting": "Healthy adult participants aged 19-42 tested in a laboratory setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 25,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Healthy participants recruited from the University of Tübingen; informed consent obtained.",
  "analysis_plan": "Repeated measures ANOVA with factors Stimulus, Site, and Time, incorporating Greenhouse-Geisser non-sphericity correction when appropriate.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Experiment 4 utilized a single phase with tone duration of 100 ms and a stimulus-onset-asynchrony of 600 ms between CS and UCS, comprising 280 standard trials and 60 trials each of CS+ and CS-."
}
